title: SG-7.10 Claude Code CLI adapter with restricted permissions and no raw community text
summary: Claude adapter runs with restricted permissions, takes only structured input, and is unit tested with a mocked executor
description: Context: backend/worker/internal/provider/claude.go already has a Claude adapter that calls an Exec interface with `claude -p <fixed prompt>`, with unit tests using a recording fake Exec. It passes no permission restrictions. Desired behavior: the adapter limits what the CLI may do, never uses a shell, and receives only a constant instruction that points at structured tasks under development/tasks, never raw community text. Expected result: unit tests with a fake Exec prove all of this. Why: community prompts are untrusted and the coding agent must run restricted.
acceptance_criteria: Given the Claude adapter, when Run is called, then the Exec receives permission-restricting flags that exclude shell and network tools
Given the Claude adapter, when Run is called, then the args contain only a fixed prompt naming development/tasks and no caller-supplied text
Given an empty work directory, when Run is called, then it returns an error and Exec is not called

preserve: Cost 0 return and error wrapping with the 'provider claude' prefix

technical_constraints: No shell: command name and args are passed to Exec as a list
Tests use a fake Exec only
definition_of_done: Adapter restricted and unit tests pass with go test ./internal/provider
non_functional: Security: untrusted community text never reaches the agent command line
